claim: Human critical-thinking instruction raises scores on standard tests by about 0.3 to 0.34 SD, with very large spread between studies.
agent_test: Treat any single instruction lever as worth about 0.3 SD; require paired runs at equal tokens before keeping any schema element (G7).

claim: The gain depends on the outcome measure: content-specific CT g=0.57 vs generic CT 0.30 vs dispositions 0.23. Tests close to the taught content show larger gains.
agent_test: Score the agent on tasks matching the taught operator vs held-out task types; expect the matched set to gain more.

claim: Human CT teaching works best when dialogue, authentic problems and mentoring are combined (g=0.57, 19 studies) versus about 0.4 for single elements.
agent_test: Compare an agent with only one of worked tasks, external critic, or lesson memory against all three at equal tokens.

claim: Stand-alone vs infused delivery makes no clear difference; the best form states abstract principles explicitly and then applies them to concrete content.
agent_test: Compare prompt with named principle then application against application alone, at equal tokens.

claim: Worked examples help human mathematics learning at a medium size (g=0.48, 55 studies); correct examples beat incorrect ones.
agent_test: Only the 2023 meta-analysis was read; the founding study a21 was not opened. Test correct vs flawed exemplars in the memory of solved problems.

claim: Showing a large LLM worked solutions with steps (chain of thought) raises accuracy on multi-step math and symbolic tasks; GSM8K 17.9 to 56.9 on PaLM 540B.
agent_test: Short step-wise reasoning vs direct answer at equal tokens on math and logic items; skip on non-symbolic items.

claim: Chain of thought gives near-zero gain outside math, logic and symbolic tasks (mean +0.7 elsewhere vs +12 to +14).
agent_test: Route by task type: apply stepwise reasoning only to symbolic or multi-step items; measure spend saved.

claim: Step-by-step instruction needs model scale: it hurts most models under 10B and helps from about 100B; explanations in context help only large models.
agent_test: Re-run each schema element on the actual base model; do not carry results from other model sizes.

claim: A bare zero-shot cue (think step by step) lifts large-model accuracy, but less than hand-written worked examples, and not on one-step tasks.
agent_test: Compare zero-shot cue, few-shot exemplars, and none at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In few-shot examples, format, label space and input distribution carry most of the benefit; correct labels matter little (1.7 to 2.6 points).
agent_test: Check whether retrieved lessons help by format or by content: swap in wrong-answer exemplars.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Which examples are shown matters: retrieving similar examples beats random (+41.9% ToTTo, +45.5% NQ), and self-generated relevant exemplars match hand-written ones.
agent_test: Retrieval of similar solved items vs random items vs self-generated analogues, equal tokens.

claim: Self-correction without an outside signal does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0). Reported gains came from oracle labels or weak baselines.
agent_test: Pair a revise-on-own-opinion arm with revise-on-failing-output arm at equal calls; expect the second to win.

claim: Multi-agent debate beat single answers and reflection in the original paper (GSM8K 77.0 to 85.0), but independent token-matched tests (Huang 2024; Zhang 2025 over 9 benchmarks and 4 models) find it rarely beats CoT or majority-vote self-consistency (significant win over CoT in about 15% of configurations).
agent_test: Spend extra compute on independent samples plus a vote, not on debate; keep any critic gated on an outside check.

claim: Persona diversity gave a small extra debate gain (MMLU 71.1 to 74.2), but persona diversity is not diversity of evidence. Mixing different base models did help debate (Heter-MAD average 76.7 vs 74.3 same-model SoM), which a single-model agent cannot copy.
agent_test: Persona agents vs same-prompt samples at equal calls; G4 predicts no gain.

claim: Earlier self-refine gains were inflated by weak baseline prompts: with a strong single-pass prompt, self-correct 75.1 vs standard 81.8 on CommonGen-Hard, costing 7 calls vs 1.
agent_test: Always tune the plain baseline before measuring a schema element.

claim: In both human and LLM literature the choice of control group moves the effect size (inquiry g 1.53 vs lecture, 0.78 vs active control).
agent_test: Report each schema gain against a tuned plain arm and an active-control arm.

claim: Chain-of-thought text can be a plausible story that does not name the real cause of the answer (accuracy drop up to 36% under biased option order).
agent_test: Plant a biasing hint; check whether the stated reasoning mentions it; decide from checks, not text.

claim: Asking first for the governing principle, then solving (step-back), helps hard STEM and multi-hop tasks (Physics +7, Chemistry +11, TimeQA +27 on PaLM-2L).
agent_test: Generalise-first prompt vs direct on hard physics and multi-hop items at equal tokens.

claim: Sequenced easy-to-hard subproblem teaching lets models solve problems harder than the examples (SCAN at least 99% vs 16%), and fully explicit algorithm teaching beats looser rationales.
agent_test: Least-to-most decomposition vs flat CoT on length-generalisation items.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Strong LLM problem-solvers are poor tutors: they reveal the answer early (66%) and give wrong feedback (59%); leakage must be penalised.
agent_test: Not an agent-schema item; relevant if the agent explains to users. Measure leakage rate.

claim: A pedagogy-structured GPT-4 tutor beat in-class active learning in one randomised crossover (median post 4.5 vs 3.5; effect 0.63 to 1.3 SD).
agent_test: One physics course, one site; a15 and c16 are the same study. No ablation of which element mattered.

claim: Unstructured LLM help raises practice scores but lowers later unassisted performance (-17%); hints plus the solution in the prompt remove most of the harm.
agent_test: Agent analogue: help that does the work removes the learning signal; test writing memory only from verified lessons.

claim: Students over-estimate what they learn from AI help (self-rated learning above measured).
agent_test: Self-report is not a measure; the agent should not trust its own confidence.

claim: AI-supported education reviews show no uniform effect: structured use helps; null or negative results appear versus established resources.
agent_test: Narrative reviews only; no pooled effect.

claim: Verbal feedback from past failures (Reflexion, ExpeL) improves agents when an external signal such as unit tests exists.
agent_test: Lesson memory with test-based gating vs ungated lessons, equal tokens.

claim: A pipeline of critical questions from argumentation theory raised MT-Bench scores slightly (6.75 to 7.3 on one model).
agent_test: Single preprint, LLM-judged scores; small gains. Compare with a plain check pass at equal tokens.

claim: Long prompts lose information in the middle; placement of lessons matters.
agent_test: Put retrieved lessons at start or end of context; test middle placement.

claim: Inquiry-based learning has pooled g=1.34 on CT tests, but with I2=92% and signs of publication bias (Egger p<.001); not a reliable estimate.
agent_test: Treat as upper bound with bias; no direct agent test.

claim: General college attendance raises CT from the 50th to the 72nd percentile over 4 years, while programs aimed at CT added no long-term extra. This sits against Abrami's positive 0.3 for direct instruction.
agent_test: No agent test; unresolved (see critique).

claim: Explicit 'think step by step' instruction adds little on current reasoning models: about +3 points or less on GPQA Diamond (o3-mini +2.9, o4-mini +3.1, Gemini Flash 2.5 -3.3) at 20-80% more time; on non-reasoning models much of the gain comes from a baseline that forbids reasoning.
agent_test: Always compare the scaffold against the model's default thinking at equal tokens; do not count a gain over a 'no thinking' baseline.

claim: Pasting worked solutions into the prompt of a reasoning model hurts it: AIME'25 1-shot drops about 6-16 points and 3-shot up to 35; GPQA 1-5 and 4-8. The cause is copying of steps. Turning the demos into abstract insights beat direct answering (AIME'25 42.0 to 48.0/51.3 on R1-Distill-7B). This is an LLM analogue of the human expertise reversal effect, but the human effect itself was not re-read.
agent_test: Test lessons as abstract rules vs full worked cases on a strong model; expect rules to win.

claim: A lesson or experience store helps only when entries are verified. Add-everything memory fell below a small fixed memory (RegAgent 55.5 vs 67.5) while oracle-gated memory was best (70.95); a coarse LLM judge fine-tuned on 300 labels recovered most of the gap. Reflection without a real test hurt (HumanEval Rust 0.52 vs 0.60 base).
agent_test: Write a lesson only after an external check passes; track later outcomes per lesson and delete the ones that fail.

claim: Agents copy near-matching stored outputs (output similarity follows input similarity, r close to 1), so one stored error spreads to later similar tasks.
agent_test: Do not retrieve near-duplicate past answers verbatim; retrieve the rule and re-derive.

claim: Unassisted discovery is worse than explicit instruction (d=-0.38, 108 studies), guided discovery is better than other methods (d=+0.30, 56 studies); worked examples (-0.63) and feedback (-0.46) beat unassisted discovery most. Guided discovery equals worked examples (0.06, ns). Domain size varies: math -0.16 to verbal -0.95.
agent_test: Give the agent a worked case plus an explanation request plus outside feedback; no-guidance self-discovery is the weak arm.

claim: In a school RCT (nearly 1,000 students) plain GPT-4 help raised practice grades 48% but cut the later unaided exam 17%; a hint-and-solution tutor prompt raised practice 127% and removed the exam loss without adding a gain. Students did not notice the loss. Numbers read from the PNAS paper; no independent replication found.
agent_test: Score the agent on unaided held-out runs after it has used memory, not only on runs that had the stored answers.

claim: The Kestin tutor result has no component ablation: prompt, enforced step order and expert solutions came together. The authors report that a system prompt alone could not hold step order, so the platform enforced it.
agent_test: Enforce state order in the harness instead of asking for it in the prompt; ablate it in a paired run.
